You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

{
 "path": "continual_arc_task-1707cc05.md",
 "content": "# Continual ARC task-1707cc05

## Rule inferred from demo and validated test
The background is color 6. There are separated horizontal runs of alternating color 1 cells, with gaps between them. Fill the intervening gaps *within each horizontal run* with color 2, alternating with the existing 1s. Do not alter rows/gaps beyond the run. Each run's sequence is 1,2,1,2,...; the demo reveals this clearly: a run of five 8s was expanded to alternating 8,2,... and longer run similarly. On test with 1s, fill the spaces between successive 1s with 2, leaving the ends and all 6 background unchanged. Solved test was accepted.

## Practical detection
For each row, identify contiguous horizontal pattern runs spanning positions that have occupied 1s every other column (possibly with missing cells at odd positions). Fill cells of color 6 between the end-to-end endpoints with 2 where alternating slots are gaps; existing 1s remain. This instance's runs have all their non-background color-1 cells at even or odd alternating columns, with row-by-row shifted alignment. Preserve spacing and do not extrapolate beyond outermost original 1s.

Demo: background 6, foreground 8 at every other position in two rows; output filled with 2 at in-between cells, other cells unchanged. Test: same transformation with foreground 1; correct output confirmed."
